_source: Transcribed from the Claude Design handoff bundle's VENUES constant in Curia.dc.html (fetched 2026-07-30) — real illustrative seed venues, not chains, matching Hard rule 1. `reason` strings are the actual brand-voice match-reason copy from the prototype; use as the register/quality bar for new copy, not verbatim filler. Added by curia-moments-journeys (M6): The Old Cellars is transcribed from the prototype's own VENUES constant (this file was previously a 15-of-18 subset that happened to omit it, even though the prototype's own moments picks reference it by name). Everyman Cinema/Rudy's/Porta are transcribed from the prototype's own JOURNEYS constant (the 'Date Night in Altrincham' stops, which carry name/kind/note there but were never given a standalone VENUES entry in the prototype) — lat/lon/spend/base/bands for those three are new, plausible fill-ins (Altrincham town centre) rather than transcribed, since the prototype never assigned them any.
_metroScopeNote: A Los Angeles metro (Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City — 31 real, independently-verified venues) existed here from an earlier 2026-08 pass and was removed at explicit later request (2026-08) to keep the app scoped to Manchester/Cheshire only. See docs/data/districts.json's own _metroScopeNote for the same removal on the district side.
_manchesterCheshireResearchSource: Happy Seasons, The Bull's Head, HOME, Band on the Wall, Manchester Art Gallery, Royal Exchange Theatre, and The Wine Cellar were added 2026-08 from the first run of the daily Manchester/Cheshire research pipeline (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md), manually reviewed and promoted (the automated review agent was down at the time — see .claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md for what that step normally does) rather than left in docs/data/venue-suggestions.json. All seven verified real, currently-operating, single-site or same-village-group venues via independent web sources (official sites, CAMRA, Tripadvisor, council/charity registries) — none are chains (Hard rule 1); The Bull's Head shares ownership with two sister pubs, both in the same village of Mobberley, the same precedent as this file's own Ivy Spinningfields/Craig's. Filled real gaps: Chinatown and Mobberley had zero prior venues, Deansgate had zero Do-category venues, and Do was the thinnest category city-wide. Happy Seasons introduced a new venue type, 'CANTONESE ROAST' (no existing Eat tile/type fit a roast-meats specialist) — mapped to the Eat category in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts so mood filtering still finds it, though no onboarding tile targets it specifically yet.
_cheshireExpansionSource: Altrincham Market, Sugo Pasta Kitchen, The Old Dancer, The Stolen Lamb, The Elk of Hale, Church Inn, and Aldeli were added 2026-08 at explicit user request to expand Cheshire's coverage, which at 8 venues across 5 districts was noticeably thinner than Manchester's. Manually researched and verified one at a time via direct web search (not the automated pipeline) — real, currently-operating, single-site or small-regional-group venues, checked against Hard rule 1 the same way as the entries above; two strong candidates (Yara, Eastern Revive) were dropped despite being independent and family-run because their 5-6-site regional footprints read closer to a small chain than a same-village group, and a third (Victors, Alderley Edge) was dropped because it's a second branch of the Hale Victors already seeded here and would have collided on the same slugified id. Church Inn is Bull's Head's actual sister pub (same Cheshire Cat Pubs & Bars group, same village) — a real instance of the ownership pattern already flagged above, not a new one; a third sibling (Roebuck Inn, also Mobberley) was found but skipped to avoid three venues from one seven-pub group sitting in a single small village. Filled real gaps: Altrincham Market gives Cheshire its first Do-category venue with real liveliness (Everyman Cinema was previously the only one); Aldeli introduces a new type, 'BRUNCH SPOT', for the 'Brunch' onboarding tile, which previously matched zero venues anywhere in the app — mapped in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts. 'ALE HOUSE' (The Old Dancer, since removed — see _closureNote below) and 'GREEK TAVERNA' (The Stolen Lamb) are also new types, left Drink/Eat category-only for now (like CANTONESE ROAST) since no existing onboarding tile fits either precisely.
_wilmslowDensitySource: 20 venues added 2026-08 at explicit user request — a deliberate density test ('so we can test how the matchmaking works close to me with a semi densely populated town'), targeting 5 Drink / 7 Eat / 10 Do specifically for Wilmslow, plus Wilmslow Golf Club (added alongside, but seeded in Mobberley — see below). Landed at 4 Drink / 7 Eat / 10 Do (21 Wilmslow venues total including the two already there) after extensive individual research: Wilmslow's bar scene turned out to be unusually chain-heavy for a Cheshire town (excluded, with real footprints checked: Slug & Lettuce, The Botanist, Revolution, Unico Lounge [part of 'The Lounges', 200+ sites], Anthology [Greene King-owned, since renamed The Swan Inn], The King William [Robinsons Brewery], Stanneylands Hotel [now JW Lees-owned, the same chain already excluded once for Alderley Edge Hotel]) — a 5th genuine independent wasn't found after a good-faith search, so 4 is the honest number rather than a padded one. Every included venue passed the same single-site/small-local-group Hard rule 1 screen as prior passes; Cibo, Suburban Green, Smoke Wilmslow, Heddy's and Caramello are all real 2-site sibling pairs (their other sites: Didsbury, Chorlton, Chorlton, Alderley Edge, Didsbury respectively) — the same precedent already established for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields/Sugo. Wilmslow Golf Club is real and genuinely called that, but its actual grounds sit in Great Warford, within Mobberley's territory, not Wilmslow's — seeded there by real location rather than by name. Closed 5 real onboarding-tile coverage gaps that had zero matching venues anywhere in the app: 'Parks & green space' (The Carrs), 'Cookery & craft' (Wilmslow Kitchen), 'Walking tours' (Wilmslow History Tours), 'Late-night lounges' (Symposium), and 'Spectator sport' (Wilmslow RUFC and Wilmslow Golf Club) — plus extended 'Markets', which already had Mackie Mayor/Altrincham Market, to its first artisan-market example (Wilmslow Artisan Market). See src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts for the mappings. Introduced 14 new venue types; most are Eat/Drink category-only (no tile fits precisely, same treatment as CANTONESE ROAST) since a small town's real venues don't sort neatly into the tile catalog's higher-end city categories.
_closureNote: The Old Dancer (16 Grove Street, Wilmslow) was removed 2026-08, one day after being added in the pass above, on direct user report that it has permanently closed — independent web sources (Yelp, Tripadvisor) still listed it as open as of this same date, so this is trusted local/current knowledge outweighing lagging listing sites, not independently re-corroborated. No dangling Moment/Journey references existed to clean up. Its 'ALE HOUSE' type mapping in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts was left in place (harmless, ready for a future venue of that type) rather than removed, matching how other now-unused-but-still-mapped types are handled. This prompted two changes to the daily research/review agent briefs (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md, .claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md): checking a candidate is real and non-chain was never the same as checking it's still open today, and neither brief previously re-verified already-promoted venues at all — see those files' own updated 'still operating' guidance. Sugo Pasta Kitchen (Altrincham) was removed 2026-09-01 by the curia-suggestion-review closure audit: it rebranded to Sud Pasta and closed all four sites nationwide on 31 Dec 2023 (thecaterer.com, Taste of Manchester), with the Altrincham address now trading as an unrelated restaurant, Rigatoni's. No dangling Moment/Journey references existed to clean up.

venues.name: Erst
venues.reason: Natural wine and communal tables both on, and the kitchen runs to 11pm.

venues.name: Schofield's
venues.reason: Award-winning list, mixology at the table — the fullest version of your cocktail tile.

venues.name: Mana
venues.reason: Michelin-recognised with a chef's table; one step above your spend dial.

venues.name: 20 Stories
venues.reason: Skyline view and heated outdoor seating — the heaters matter tonight.

venues.name: The Jane Eyre
venues.reason: Booth seating and no music you have to shout over.

venues.name: Blinker
venues.reason: Unmarked entrance on Tib Street; speakeasy-style still weighted on.

venues.name: Matt & Phreds
venues.reason: Live sets to 1am, intimate seating, no cover before nine.

venues.name: The Ivy Spinningfields
venues.reason: Formal service and a dress code; late sittings to 10.30pm.

venues.name: Refuge
venues.reason: Live pianist Thursday to Saturday, service well past midnight.

venues.name: Tattu
venues.reason: Set menus and dessert theatrics; loudest room in the district after nine.

venues.name: Victors
venues.reason: Communal tables on, group-friendly buzz — worth the drive on a Friday.

venues.name: Pollen Bakery
venues.reason: Canalside counter seats and viennoiserie out of the oven at eight.

venues.name: Mackie Mayor
venues.reason: Nine kitchens under one roof — the easiest room in the city to arrive at without a plan.

venues.name: Foundation Coffee
venues.reason: A mill floor big enough to work in, and nobody rushing the second cup.

venues.name: The Wizard
venues.reason: Fires lit from October, and the Edge walk finishes at the door.

venues.name: The Old Cellars
venues.reason: Sommelier on site and small plates until close.

venues.name: Everyman Cinema
venues.reason: Sofa seats in screen two. Order the wine before the trailers — they bring it to you.

venues.name: Rudy's
venues.reason: No bookings, but the queue after the late screening is usually nothing.

venues.name: Porta
venues.reason: One last sherry standing at the counter. Kitchen closes at midnight.

venues.name: Happy Seasons
venues.reason: Forty-odd years on Faulkner Street, and the queue for the roast duck still forms before the doors do.

venues.name: The Bull's Head
venues.reason: Named best pub in Cheshire, then best in the whole North West, and Mill Lane still has more sheep on it than sat-nav.

venues.name: HOME
venues.reason: Five screens, two stages and a gallery floor that's changed again by the time you've finished your coffee downstairs.

venues.name: Band on the Wall
venues.reason: A stage bolted high on the far wall since the thirties, reborn after a £3.5m rebuild — the room where the touring act you half-recognise turns out to be the whole point of the night.

venues.name: Manchester Art Gallery
venues.reason: Free to walk in off Mosley Street and stand in front of the Pre-Raphaelites; the current dress-and-textile show, WORN, quietly reframes how you look at your own coat on the way out.

venues.name: Royal Exchange Theatre
venues.reason: A glass module dropped into a Victorian trading hall — the largest theatre-in-the-round in the world, close enough that the actors' footsteps land in your chest.

venues.name: The Wine Cellar
venues.reason: Forty wines by the glass and a slate of Courtyard Dairy cheese on a Hawthorn Lane side street — the sort of place you mean to leave after one and don't.

venues.name: Altrincham Market
venues.reason: Ten independent kitchens and two bars under one market roof, open till ten most nights — arrive hungry and undecided, leave neither.

venues.name: The Stolen Lamb
venues.reason: Chef-owned Greek on Water Lane, island-leaning rather than taverna-cliché — the lamb chops are why regulars stopped reading past them.

venues.name: Suburban Green
venues.reason: Sister site to the Chorlton original, four doors down Hawthorn Lane from its own sibling Wine Cellar — small plates built to share and a list that never repeats a wine twice a week.

venues.name: Smoke Wilmslow
venues.reason: Four generations of curing and smoking behind the bar snacks — Water Lane's café by day, cocktail room by night, same kitchen either way.

venues.name: Symposium
venues.reason: Grove Street's latest late licence — upstairs booths built for the hour after everywhere else has called last orders.

venues.name: Cibo
venues.reason: Family-run on Green Lane, a retractable roof over the terrace and a hundred and sixty covers that still feel like a neighbourhood table.

venues.name: Heddy's
venues.reason: Water Lane institution now with a second room in Alderley Edge — the mezze arrives before you've finished deciding what else to order.

venues.name: Caramello
venues.reason: Didsbury's original brunch room found a second home on Water Lane — scratch-made plates and a queue that starts before ten.

venues.name: Wilmslow Tavern
venues.reason: Simon and Kay's village-centre local out toward Dean Row — proper pizza, a beer garden, and nobody rushing you off the table.

venues.name: Phanthong Thai
venues.reason: Mum-and-daughter run on Alderley Road, next door to the King's Arms — the menu reads long and somehow everything on it is right.

venues.name: Vietbowl
venues.reason: Family-run home-style cooking on Bank Square — the kind of pho you'd get told to slow down and finish properly.

venues.name: Rex Cinema
venues.reason: Art deco since 1936, dark for two decades, reborn in 2019 — plush seats, a proper bar, and the original REX signage still over the door.

venues.name: The Carrs
venues.reason: Seventy-one acres along the Bollin, gifted to the town by a Boddington and named for the Norse word for bog-meadow — the walk that clears a working week.

venues.name: Wilmslow Kitchen
venues.reason: Sarah and David Bridge's school on the Deanway estate, tucked behind a row of Ferrari and Porsche showrooms — evening classes end with everyone sitting down to eat what they made.

venues.name: Ricardo Van Parmar Gallery
venues.reason: Private viewings by appointment on Alderley Road — the stock runs from emerging names to originals by Banksy and Warhol, and nobody hurries you round.

venues.name: Wilmslow Artisan Market
venues.reason: Grove Street and Bank Square close to traffic once a month for a hundred stalls of food, craft and live music — check the date before you plan an evening around it.

venues.name: Wilmslow RUFC
venues.reason: Memorial Ground on Kings Road, a co-operatively owned club pitched between the Carrs and the river — North West 1 rugby with a proper clubhouse pint after.

venues.name: Green Room Theatre
venues.reason: A Victorian cottage and an old shirt factory, converted by the town's own amateur society — founded in 1924, one of the oldest in the country, and still selling out a hundred-and-two-seat house.

venues.name: Wilmslow Pilates & Wellness
venues.reason: Above a bakery on Hawthorn Lane, the same studio Tracey has taught from for over twenty years — small classes, monthly sound ceremonies, no scale in sight.

venues.name: Wilmslow History Tours
venues.reason: Free, two hours, departs the library at eleven — the Historical Society's own guide walks you into St Bartholomew's, on a site with a church since 1246.

venues.name: Alchemy Personal Training
venues.reason: A private studio off Hawthorn Walk, wet room and changing rooms included — one-to-one sessions, not a class timetable to fit yourself around.

venues.name: Wilmslow Golf Club
venues.reason: Great Warford's eighteen holes since the 1880s, shaped in turn by James Braid and Frederick Hawtree — Open qualifying history on a course most of Cheshire only plays as a guest.

venues.name: The Elk of Hale
venues.reason: Family-run since 2013 on Ashley Road, an Alpine-lodge fit-out that shouldn't work in Cheshire and does — the spirits list runs deeper than the room.

venues.name: Church Inn
venues.reason: Opposite the twelfth-century church it's named for, and named best pub in the country more than once since — book the snug or don't bother.

venues.name: Aldeli
venues.reason: A former car showroom turned New York deli on London Road — salt beef bagels before noon, pancakes after.

venues.name: Hallé St Peter's
venues.reason: A deconsecrated Grade II church on Blossom Street, still the Hallé's own rehearsal hall — public concerts land in a room built for hymn acoustics, not a sound engineer.

venues.name: BAB NQ
venues.reason: Flatbreads made from scratch in an open theatre kitchen, and a basement cocktail room that only unlocks once the sun's properly down.

venues.name: Smolensky Gallery
venues.reason: Polished concrete and street-art pedigree inside the ABC Building on Quay Street — worth a detour on the way to dinner, not an afterthought once you've eaten.

venues.name: Podium Restaurant
venues.reason: Two AA Rosettes some forty floors below Cloud 23, and a kitchen more assured than the view it's sitting under.

venues.name: Hale Country Club & Spa
venues.reason: Five thermal rooms and an infinity pool looking out over its own acreage of Cheshire countryside — a members' club that still takes you for the day.

venues.name: The Yard
venues.reason: A greengrocer, a bakery and a juice bar built round a shared courtyard since 2012 — market-hall energy squeezed onto a converted Cheshire builder's plot.

venues.name: Barnshaw Smithy
venues.reason: Poached eggs and proper coffee next to a working reclamation yard, on the lane between Mobberley and Ashley that the sat-nav still hesitates over.

venues.name: Nam
venues.reason: Manchester's only true audiophile sound system, assembled by the team behind London's Brilliant Corners, running in the basement of a Vietnamese kitchen that keeps going long after the DJs start.

venues.name: ATOMECA Wine Bar
venues.reason: Schofield's own second act on The Avenue — a walk-in wine list built around small plates, not the cocktail menu working next door.

venues.name: Riva Bar & Restaurant
venues.reason: Cecil Road's quieter answer to Hale's louder terraces — a proper wine list, unhurried service, and a Sunday lunch regulars book a week out for.

venues.name: Hope Mill Theatre
venues.reason: A converted cotton mill on Pollard Street, opened by two directors chasing Off West End intimacy — Fringe Venue of the Year, and every seat close enough to see the actors breathe.

venues.name: Another Hand
venues.reason: Twenty-four covers up a flight of painted steps on Deansgate Mews, low-intervention plates built around whatever Cinderwood's growers sent over that morning.

venues.name: King Street Townhouse Spa
venues.reason: A subterranean ESPA spa under a Grade II Italianate former bank on King Street, Himalayan salt cave included — the infinity pool upstairs is for residents, the day spa isn't.

venues.name: Evelyn's Cafe Bar
venues.reason: Brunch classics by day, then the charcoal Inka grill takes over after dark — Persian and Pan-Asian small plates in a room that never quite decides which meal it's for, on purpose.

venues.name: Waugh Brow Farm Shop
venues.reason: Dave and Ruth Jones's own cattle and pigs, twenty yards from the counter that sells them — a working farm since 1985, with a café tacked on for people who came for bacon and stayed for cake.

venues.name: Flawd Wine
venues.reason: A waterside bottle shop on the New Islington marina that doubles as a bar — walk-ins only, a cheese board built to match whatever's open, and a wine list that skips anything you'd call conventional.

venues.name: Reserve at The Rex
venues.reason: Three separate terraces above a former bank on King Street, each with its own name and its own hour of the day it does best — arrive before the swing band starts if you want a seat outside.

venues.name: Riddles
venues.reason: A 1920s room the size of a living room on Greenwood Street, yards from the market — Emma's own list of Prohibition-era cocktails, poured by people who mean it.

venues.name: Speak In Code
venues.reason: No sign on Jackson's Row, just a door — inside, entirely plant-based small plates and a cocktail list built on the bar's own fermentations, running to 2am.

venues.name: Bar Shrimp
venues.reason: Seafood snacks and cocktails under one mood-lit roof on New York Street, built by the Higher Ground and Flawd team around a sound system that does as much of the work as the bar.

venues.name: Manchester Rare Books
venues.reason: A former waiting room on platform one, stocked with pre-loved and hard-to-find titles, plus a shelf of film and music ephemera nobody's rushing you to buy.

venues.name: Charlie Brown's Hale
venues.reason: The former GupShup site on Ashley Road, made over into a corner gastro bar — signature cocktails alongside the food, for once, rather than an afterthought.

venues.name: esea contemporary
venues.reason: The UK's only art centre built around East and Southeast Asian practice, in an RIBA award-winning Market Buildings conversion on Thomas Street — free to walk into, and worth the detour even mid-crawl.

venues.name: Mobberley Cricket Club
venues.reason: Founded 1876, still on Church Lane — a clubhouse bar and a viewing rail looking out over a Cheshire outfield, the same unhurried afternoon it's always been.

moments.title: Best for Date Night
moments.blurb: Low light, tables for two, and a wine list worth staying for a third glass.

moments.title: Entertaining a Client
moments.blurb: Quiet enough to talk. Expensive enough to register without being said out loud.

moments.title: Big Group of Friends
moments.blurb: Rooms that can take eight at short notice without a sigh from the host.

moments.title: Solo Reset
moments.blurb: Counter seats, a book, and nobody asking whether you're waiting for someone.

journeys.title: Date Night in Altrincham
journeys.blurb: A film first so there's something to talk about, then eight minutes on foot to the best pizza in the county.

journeys.title: A Client, Well Handled
journeys.blurb: Height first for the view, then somewhere with tablecloths and a sommelier who knows when to leave you alone.
